raceHistory: 4 years recreational running before this plan
Mid-plan 5K time trial during Week 6 build
5K race: 24:51 on 2026-08-30 (goal was sub-25:00) — negative split, HR stayed below LTHR through km 4

currentForm.timeSincePeakFitness: 0 weeks — race just completed, this plan starts 1 week post-race

strengths.evidence: Disciplined pacing and negative-split execution on race day; cadence improved to 168-176spm; HR control shows real aerobic + threshold development from the last 10 weeks

limiters.evidence: Original limiter was inconsistent training frequency — resolved during the race build, but staying consistent with only 2-3 flexible sessions/week through a busier, colder, wetter season is the risk this plan is designed around

constraints: 2-3 runs/week capacity, no fixed days — work schedule varies week to week
Entering the cooler, wetter part of the year
No goal race currently scheduled — this is a maintenance, not a build, block
Racing a 4-mile turkey trot on 2026-11-26 (unplanned mid-block) — Week 12 restructured around it

hr.notes: Updated from LTHR ~165 to ~158, based on the Jul 31 time trial (25:47, avg HR 158, max 166) and the Aug 30 race (24:51, HR up to 166 sustained through km 5 at all-out effort). The original 165 estimate came from a single early training run and was consistently too high across every hard effort since.

pace.notes: Rebuilt around the diary's 5-tier system (E/M/T/I/R), anchored on Threshold pace — the most directly measured number, taken from the Jul 31 time trial run essentially at LTHR (158bpm) for 25+ minutes. Interval pace is validated by the actual VO2max session (4:47-5:04/km) and the race's middle kilometers (4:55/km). Easy pace is intentionally slower than recent training runs (5:36-6:00/km) — those were drifting toward Marathon-pace territory rather than true easy; the workouts below use true Easy pace.
pace.marathon: 5:20-5:30/km (speculative — no marathon-distance data yet; would need a long tempo effort or race to validate)
pace.repetition: 4:30-4:45/km (not currently used by any session in this plan)

phases.name: Recovery
phases.focus: Post-race deload before maintenance training resumes
keyWorkouts: Very easy shakeout runs, no pace targets
physiologicalGoals: Full muscular and CNS recovery before resuming structure

phases.name: Maintenance Cycle 1
phases.focus: Sustain aerobic base and threshold fitness with minimal, flexible structure
keyWorkouts: One tempo or interval session per week (alternating)
physiologicalGoals: Hold LTHR and running economy near race-week levels
Keep just enough top-end stimulus that VO2max doesn't decay
Protect training consistency through schedule and weather disruption

phases.name: Maintenance Cycle 2 (repeat)
phases.focus: Exact repeat of Cycle 1's template — same weekly pattern, re-applied
keyWorkouts: One tempo or interval session per week (alternating)
physiologicalGoals: Sustain fitness through the darkest/wettest months
Keep the habit consistent regardless of weather — this is the whole point of the block

workouts.name: Rest Day (light strength only)
workouts.description: Race is tomorrow — skip the usual paired run this week and go easy on the strength session too: keep loads moderate, skip anything maximal, and prioritize leaving the legs fresh over the session itself. If you can shift heavier lifting to earlier in the week just this once, that's even better.

workouts.name: 🦃 4-Mile Race (Turkey Trot)
workouts.description: Race day. This isn't a goal race for this block, but since you're racing anyway, run it for real — it doubles as this week's hard effort. Based on your 24:51 5K (Aug 30), a fitness-equivalent 4-mile effort predicts roughly 32:00-33:00, i.e. 5:00-5:10/km (8:03-8:19/mi). Treat that as a guide, not a mandate — maintenance-phase fitness may be a touch below your race-peak, so run by feel (hard but controlled, 7-8/10) and let the watch confirm rather than dictate. Same pacing discipline as your 5K: don't go out too hot in the first mile.
workouts.humanReadable:
Warm-up: 10-15min easy jog + 4x100m strides
Race: 4mi (6.44km) @ ~5:00-5:10/km (8:03-8:19/mi), controlled start, hold through the middle, push if it's there in the last mile
Cool-down: 10min easy walk/jog
No formal taper needed for this one — Tuesday and Wednesday are already doing that job.

run.notes: If you register a race mid-cycle, treat that week as a one-off cutback + effort, using the same pacing discipline from your sub-25 race: slightly conservative km1, even through the middle, push the last km.

nutrition.preRace: Not applicable during maintenance — normal eating.
nutrition.notes: No race-day fueling needed for these sessions; just normal hydration, more so on longer steady runs in the heat... or, this time of year, layered up in the cold.

taper.notes: No taper needed — this is a repeating maintenance cycle, not a race build. If you decide to target a new race, tell me and I'll build a proper build/peak/taper plan from wherever your fitness is at that point.
